# `request-body-added-optional`

Optional request body added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `request-body-added-optional` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Request bodies ([RULES.md section 5](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An operation that had no request body now accepts an optional one.

## Why this default

Old clients send no body, which is still valid.

## Example

From test case [`request-body-added-optional`](../../test/cases/request-body-added-optional/): An optional body where there was none.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
      post:
        operationId: createPet
+       requestBody:
+         content:
+           application/json:
+             schema:
+               type: object
        responses:
          '200':
```

Findings:

- `request-body-added-optional` · info · POST /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  request-body-added-optional: info
```
